domains.tagline: Chemical dependencies — from stimulants to sedatives.

domains.name: Mental Health & Distress

modules.title: Assessment & Readiness for Change
modules.goal: Establish exact baseline intake, financial cost, and the client’s position on the Stages of Change model.
modules.body:
1. Quantify usage. Ask directly, without judgement: "How many bottles or caps do you take in 24 hours? What time is your first dose?"
  2. Identify secondary mixes. Check for combination with alcohol, sedatives, or soft drinks (lean / dirty sprite).
  3. Assess readiness (1–10). "How important is it for you to stop today, and how confident are you that you can reduce it?"
"Codeine creates physical dependence very quickly. If we stop suddenly without a plan, your body will react with restless legs, stomach cramps, and anxiety. Our goal isn't to punish you — it's to gradually take back control of your brain's opioid receptors, safely."

modules.title: Tapering & Physical Step-Down Schedule
modules.goal: Execute a structured 3-week reduction to prevent severe opiate withdrawal while steadily lowering tolerance.
modules.body:
WeekTargetOversight action
1 — StabiliseCut 25%. Eliminate evening "comfort" doses.Transfer bottle control to a trusted family member; measure exact doses with a medical cup.
2 — Step-downCut to 50% of baseline. One dose daily (afternoon).2–3L water/day. Add vitamin B-complex & magnesium for cramps.
3 — Elimination10% for 3 days, then complete cessation.Monitor sweating, diarrhoea, insomnia. Non-codeine OTC pain relief only.

Environmental cleanout: search room, bag, and phone contacts to remove empty bottles, syrup dealers, and mixing agents.

modules.title: Trigger Management & Urge Surfing
modules.goal: Train the client to ride out chemical cravings — which peak in 10–15 minutes and subside if un-fed — without giving in.
modules.body:
1. Notice. "My brain is asking for Bronco right now."
  2. Pause. Set a 15-minute timer before acting on any urge.
  3. Breathe. 4-7-8 diaphragmatic breathing to down-regulate nervous system distress.
  4. Ground. Feet flat on the floor; name 5 objects in the room.
  5. Substitute. Ice-cold water or a strong peppermint for sensory throat feedback.

modules.title: Long-Term Cessation & Life Reconstruction
modules.goal: Build alternative non-chemical reward structures and repair social networks.
modules.body:
1. Peer separation. Block and delete "sip culture" peer groups from phone and social media.
  2. Routine replacement. Fill former usage hours with mandatory physical activity — sport, gym, apprenticeship.
  3. Relapse protocol. A slip-up is a lapse to learn from, not a failure. Re-evaluate triggers immediately, without shame.

modules.title: Assessment & Readiness for Change
modules.goal: Quantify debt severity, identify emotional triggers, and break the "chasing losses" cycle.
modules.body:
• "How much have you deposited into betting apps over the last 30 days?"
  • "Have you borrowed money from loan sharks, family, or work to bet?"
  • "What thoughts run through your mind right after losing a ticket?"
Betting apps are engineered algorithms designed to extract capital — not wealth-generation platforms.

modules.title: Digital Friction & Financial Lockout
modules.goal: Systematically strip away the technical ability to place a bet within 60 seconds.
modules.body:
1. Self-exclusion. Formal closure on every active betting account — minimum 6–12 month lock.
  2. App removal. Delete apps, shortcuts, and any saved browser passwords.
  3. Financial delegation. Hand mobile-money PINs to a non-gambling relative for 90 days.

modules.title: Trigger Management & Cognitive Reframing
modules.goal: Dismantle gambling cognitive distortions before they trigger the next bet.
modules.body:
DistortionReframe
"I almost won — it crashed at 1.99x right after I tapped."A near-miss is a 100% loss by design. The crash point was set before the round began.
"I just need one big win to clear my debts."Every dollar in a negative-expectation game expands the debt. You cannot bet your way out of a gambling loss.

When the urge strikes during a live match, watch it in a public family space, without a phone present.

modules.title: Long-Term Cessation & Financial Recovery
modules.goal: Structure a concrete debt-repayment plan and rebuild healthy dopamine baselines.
modules.body:
1. Debt staging. List debts smallest to largest. Fixed, small repayments from earned income only — never from prospective winnings.
  2. Skill-based focus. Re-channel speculation energy into real-economy skills — trade, agriculture, buying/selling physical goods.
  3. Accountability partner. Daily 8pm check-in: "Day X — no bets placed, phone locked."

modules.title: Assessment & Physiological Profiling
modules.goal: Distinguish physical anxiety symptoms from medical issues and map the client’s internal "worry loops."
modules.body:
Somatic manifestations: palpitations, shallow breathing, feeling hot/shaky, stomach tightness, constant dread of impending disaster.

Your brain's alarm system is misfiring — it's treating everyday thoughts as if a wild animal is attacking you. Your racing heart and tight stomach are adrenaline signals, not signs you're dying or going crazy.

modules.title: Somatic Regulation & De-escalation
modules.goal: Teach immediate physical grounding skills that shut off the fight-or-flight response.
modules.body:
1. Physiological sigh. Two inhales through the nose, one long exhale through the mouth.
  2. Cold-water shift. Splash ice water on the face or hold an ice cube.
  3. 5-4-3-2-1 grounding. 5 things you see, 4 you touch, 3 you hear, 2 you smell, 1 you taste.

In-session: 3 minutes of box breathing (inhale 4s, hold 4s, exhale 4s, hold 4s) until heart rate visibly drops.

modules.title: Cognitive Decoupling & Worry Exposure
modules.goal: Break the habit of continuous overthinking using structured Worry Postponement.
modules.body:
1. Identify. "Is this a problem I can solve right now, or an uncertain future scenario?"
  2. Postpone. "I'm not ignoring this — I'll process it during Worry Time at 4:00pm for 15 minutes."
  3. Execute. At 4pm, write worries down for 15 minutes; cross out what can't be controlled. When the timer rings, close the notebook and change location.

modules.title: Long-Term Coping & Resilience Building
modules.goal: Build lifestyle structures that prevent baseline anxiety spikes.
modules.body:
• Stimulant removal. Cut energy drinks, high caffeine, and nicotine — they mimic anxiety adrenaline.
  • Problem-Solving Therapy. Break overwhelming stressors into single, actionable 3-step tasks.
  • Daily grounding. 15 minutes of sunlight, daily walking, fixed sleep schedule.

modules.title: Assessment & Readiness
modules.goal: Understand the current depth of the depressive cycle and where energy sits today.
modules.body:
The depression cycle: a trigger or low mood causes withdrawal and reduced activity → loss of positive reinforcement → negative thinking loops → deepened guilt and worthlessness → mood drops further.

Understanding this as a chemical and behavioural loop — not a character flaw — is the first step. Low energy is a symptom, not evidence of failure.

modules.title: Behavioural Activation
modules.goal: Break the cycle at the "reduced activity" stage — action before motivation.
modules.body:
The key principle: waiting to feel motivated rarely works, because motivation relies on dopamine, which is depleted during depression. Instead: behaviour first, then a small dopamine pulse, then motivation follows.

Micro-tasks reduce effort to near-zero — sitting on the edge of the bed for 30 seconds, opening the curtains, putting on socks, drinking half a glass of water.

After any micro-task: acknowledge the win first, then offer a low-pressure choice — "Claim win for today" or "Add one micro-step." Full permission to stop prevents overwhelm.

modules.title: Trigger Management & Cognitive Reframing
modules.goal: Catch Automatic Negative Thoughts (ANTs) before they deepen the loop.
modules.body:
1. Capture the thought. e.g. "I ruin everything I try."
  2. Name the distortion. All-or-nothing thinking, catastrophising, filtering out the good, self-labelling.
  3. Evidence check. Find evidence against the thought and write a grounded alternative.

modules.title: Long-Term Cessation & Re-Integration
modules.goal: Move from micro-tasks to graded, sustainable routines without a sudden jump in difficulty.
modules.body:
Readiness signals: consistency over motivation (3–5 days of micro-tasks regardless of mood), spontaneous momentum (adding a step unprompted), lowered resistance in check-ins.

Graded Task Assignment example — a 10-minute walk: Step 1, stand at the door for 2 minutes; Step 2, walk to the gate and back; Step 3, the full walk. If a step feels too heavy, scale back to the previous step — never treat it as a setback.

Early warning signs to watch for: shifted sleep patterns, micro-withdrawal from friends and hygiene, cognitive fog on simple decisions. When spotted, activate a pre-planned Low-Energy Protocol: one pre-written check-in text, a minimal 2-item baseline, and 60 seconds of passive sensory reset.

substances.title: Assessment & Readiness for Change
substances.goal: Establish an honest baseline of use, frequency, and the client’s readiness to change.
substances.body:
1. Quantify use. Ask what, how much, and how often — without judgement.
  2. Check for mixing. Identify any other substances used alongside this one.
  3. Readiness scale (1–10). How important is stopping today, and how confident do they feel?
Dependence is a physiological and psychological adaptation, not a moral failing. The goal is steady, safe reduction — not punishment.

substances.title: Tapering, Friction & Step-Down
substances.goal: Reduce intake gradually over a structured multi-week schedule to minimise withdrawal risk.
substances.body:
PhaseTargetSupport action
Week 1Cut ~25% of baselineRemove easiest access point; involve a support person.
Week 2Cut to ~50%Increase hydration and nutrition; monitor sleep.
Week 3Taper to full cessationWatch for withdrawal signs; seek medical support if severe.

Where physical dependence is significant, a medical or clinic-supervised taper is the safest route.

substances.title: Trigger Management & Urge Surfing
substances.goal: Ride out cravings using the wave model — they peak in 10–15 minutes and pass if un-fed.
substances.body:
1. Notice the urge without judgement.
  2. Pause — set a 15-minute timer before acting.
  3. Breathe — 4-7-8 breathing to calm the nervous system.
  4. Ground — name 5 things you can see.
  5. Substitute — cold water, movement, or a trusted call.

substances.title: Long-Term Cessation & Re-Integration
substances.goal: Rebuild a life structure that doesn’t depend on the substance for reward or coping.
substances.body:
1. Environment cleanout. Remove paraphernalia, contacts, and access points.
  2. Routine replacement. Fill former-use hours with structured activity.
  3. Relapse protocol. Treat any slip as a lapse to learn from, not a failure — reassess triggers immediately.

conditioning.title: Assessment & Readiness for Change
conditioning.goal: Quantify the scale of the behaviour and identify its emotional drivers.
conditioning.body:
• "How much time or money has this taken in the last 30 days?"
  • "What feeling shows up right before you start?"
  • "What happens in your mind right after you stop?"
These platforms are engineered for engagement, not for your wellbeing. Naming the design is the first step to resisting it.

conditioning.title: Digital Friction & Behavioural Lockout
conditioning.goal: Add deliberate friction between the impulse and the action.
conditioning.body:
1. Self-exclude / uninstall. Remove the app, or use a formal exclusion feature where available.
  2. Add a barrier. App blockers, delayed launch timers, or a trusted person holding a password.
  3. Financial or time delegation. Where money is involved, hand control to a trusted person temporarily.

conditioning.title: Trigger Management & Cognitive Reframing
conditioning.goal: Interrupt the automatic thoughts that justify "just one more."
conditioning.body:
Common distortion: "I'm due for a win / this time is different." Reframe: outcomes here are engineered, not earned — the pattern doesn't owe you anything.

When the urge strikes, change location and remove the device from reach before deciding.

conditioning.title: Long-Term Cessation & Re-Integration
conditioning.goal: Replace the behaviour’s function with healthier reward sources.
conditioning.body:
1. Identify the function the behaviour served — boredom relief, escape, social connection — and find a substitute.
  2. Rebuild routine around the freed-up time.
  3. Accountability check-in with a trusted person on a fixed schedule.

mental.title: Assessment & Readiness
mental.goal: Understand current symptom severity and physiological presentation.
mental.body:
Distinguish physical symptoms from other medical causes, and map how the distress shows up day to day — thoughts, body sensations, and behaviour.

What you're feeling has a physiological basis. Understanding the mechanism helps take away the shame.

mental.title: Stabilisation & Regulation
mental.goal: Introduce grounding and regulation tools appropriate to this condition.
mental.body:
1. Grounding. 5-4-3-2-1 sensory check-in.
  2. Breath regulation. Box breathing — inhale 4s, hold 4s, exhale 4s, hold 4s.
  3. Structure. Small, predictable daily anchors — sleep, food, light.

mental.title: Trigger Management
mental.goal: Identify and prepare for known triggers before they escalate.
mental.body: Map situations, thoughts, or sensations that reliably precede a flare. Build a simple, pre-agreed response plan for each — not a plan made in the moment.

mental.title: Long-Term Recovery & Resilience
mental.body:
• Early warning signs. Sleep shifts, withdrawal from contact, rising cognitive fog.
  • Low-energy protocol. A pre-agreed minimal baseline for hard days.
  • Professional support. Ongoing contact with a counsellor, clinic, or trusted supporter.

riskProtocol.title: Emergency Crisis Protocol
riskProtocol.body: Remove immediate lethal means. Stay with the person continuously. Escort to the nearest clinic or hospital, or contact local emergency services immediately.

distortionChips.name: All-or-Nothing
distortionChips.desc: "If it isn’t perfect, it’s a complete failure."

distortionChips.name: Fortune Telling
distortionChips.desc: "Assuming the worst outcome will happen, without proof."

distortionChips.name: Filter Out the Good
distortionChips.desc: "Focusing entirely on one bad detail, ignoring the rest."

distortionChips.name: Self-Labelling
distortionChips.desc: "Calling yourself ‘worthless’ instead of naming a mistake."

distortionChips.name: Catastrophising
distortionChips.desc: "Jumping straight to the worst possible ending."

distortionChips.name: Mind Reading
distortionChips.desc: "Assuming you know what others think of you."
